verdicts.note: Stress markers and pregnancy wastage; null, IVF setting.
Deprivation and stillbirth across 280,757 Cumbrian births 1950-92. A four-decade individual-level historical series spanning the end of the FDT.
Ethnic origin and late mid-trimester loss, Birmingham.
Life-event stress and spontaneous abortion, nested case-control.
Gestational weight gain and the SEX RATIO of births; the outcome is composition, not the count. Routes toward A.10.
Multi-omics biomarker discovery for early loss.

Historical Swedish population: inbreeding against longevity, FERTILITY and impairments, exploiting the 1844 legalisation of consanguineous marriage. Fertility is the outcome and elevated fetal loss is the presumed channel, so the channel needs confirming at full text -- but the design and period are the chapter's.
Great Leap famine and SEX RATIO at birth; difference-in-differences, but the outcome is composition. Sibling to the Cai and Wang anchor and routes to A.10.
JAMA: loss rates after ultrasound-proved viability, with pregnancies identified within 21 days of conception. Fixes the loss rate to a defined observation window.
Dutch Hunger Winter and the sex ratio; null result, but the outcome is composition.

Food shortage and human reproduction: the post-war Dresden fertility decline attributed to a food-supply collapse, with concurrent epidemics of miscarriage and low birthweight. A famine shock with a BIRTHS outcome and the loss channel named.

Population Studies: Dutch famine 1944-45 against age-specific mortality with STILLBIRTHS as a distinct age group, on 1935-47 vital statistics. Famine shock, loss outcome, and it respects the live-birth boundary.
Biomedical and Demographic Determinants of Reproduction (1993 volume), covering conception and fetal loss inside a fertility framework. FOURTH book recovered through the citation frame.
Consanguinity and reproductive consequences across 7,312 Bangladeshi families.

Social Biology 1989: loss probability by maternal age, gravidity and spacing across EIGHT World Fertility Survey countries. The multi-country demographic estimate of the loss schedule, and a companion to the Casterline measurement anchor built on the same surveys.
Risk factors in miscarriage; review, no abstract.
Socioeconomic status and stillbirth risk in Sweden, with mediation analysis.

Journal of Health Economics: civil conflict and gender-specific fetal loss, framed as a selection test. An economics-grade identification strategy on exactly B.5's channel; no abstract in the index, so retrieval is a priority.
Human embryonic and fetal death (Academic Press, 1980). The classic monograph on the loss schedule; carried keyed on title.

Population Studies 1976: facts and ARTIFACTS in the study of intra-uterine mortality, separating real variation from artefacts of data collection and of induced-abortion under-reporting. This is Wall 4 and the measurement caution stated in the demographic literature's own terms, and it predates Casterline.
Male age and spontaneous abortion controlling for female age; cross-file A.16.
Spontaneous abortion in Bahrain five years before and after the 1991 Gulf War. A war shock on the loss margin.
Demography: fetal-loss trajectories across 555,038 Czech pregnancies, with survival differentials by social position narrowing toward term. Gestational-age-resolved loss hazards at national scale.
Biological Causes of Foetal Loss: the frequency of wastage by gestational stage, including pre-recognition loss. Chapter of the 1993 volume above.
HLA-G promoter variation and miscarriage rates.

Statistical treatment of repeated pregnancy outcomes and HLA sharing in the Hutterites. Methodologically useful: repeated observations per couple are the structure every loss-and-fertility analysis has to handle.
Genetic and metabolic causes of stillbirth; review.

Stressful life events and CHROMOSOMALLY NORMAL spontaneous abortion. Conditioning on karyotype separates selection-driven loss from environmentally driven loss, which is what SELECTION_VIABILITY needs.
Spontaneous loss rates to 28 weeks in a non-selected low-risk population after confirmed viability.
Stress and immune mediators in miscarriage.
Paternity confidence and pregnancy outcomes.

Annals of Internal Medicine: maternal influenza-like illness during the 1918 pandemic against pregnancy outcomes, from 2,177 Lausanne birth records. Individual-level historical records for the 1918 shock.
Meta-analysis of influenza A in pregnancy and stillbirth risk. A pooled estimate for the epidemic channel.
Influenza death rates among pregnant women; correspondence.
Placental pathways of haemorrhagic-fever viruses.
HLA-G allele transcription rates in a cell line.
Stress and pregnancy loss review.
Consanguinity in global perspective, including reproductive wastage; review.
Consanguinity and reproductive wastage in Muslim communities; weak venue.
Influenza in pregnant PIGTAIL MACAQUES. Wall 7.
Anorexia nervosa and pregnancy outcomes across 2,134,945 Quebec pregnancies. The undernutrition channel at population scale in a modern setting.
Nepal Maoist insurgency and fetal health, conflict intensity by district and month. Conflict shock with in-utero outcomes; working paper, so the version of record needs checking.
Influenza vaccination in pregnancy.
Iranian ecological study of consanguinity against early death (stillbirth plus infant death). Composite crosses the live-birth boundary.
Reproduction and immunity in a cyprinid FISH. Wall 7.
Hormonal mechanisms in respiratory-virus outcomes.
Maternal influenza vaccination.
Progesterone and innate immunity in vitro.

American Journal of Epidemiology: national economic downturns and spontaneous pregnancy loss in Denmark, treating recession as an ambient unexpected stressor. A population-level shock with high-quality registry outcomes, and one of the few economic-shock designs on this channel.
